rationale: The workflow runs `npm ci` in three independent jobs (Lint, Test, Build) on every push and pull request, downloading dependencies each time. Adding npm dependency caching via `actions/cache@v4` with a key based on `package-lock.json` reuses the downloaded package tarballs (~/.npm) across workflow runs, reducing redundant network I/O and installation time. This matches the P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (cache dependency downloads) which has experimental evidence showing measurable VM time reduction (6% for free runners) and the provided Go-module caching example demonstrating the same mechanism for a different ecosystem. The repository has a stable `package-lock.json` (lockfileVersion 3) satisfying the pattern's preconditions of measurable repeated fetching and lockfile-based cache keys. No existing cache is present, and the cache content is immutable per lockfile, avoiding the contraindications.
